chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When it is the Day of Tarwiah, if God wills, perform ghusl, then wear your two garments (ihram), and enter the mosque barefoot, with calmness and dignity upon you. Then pray two rak'ahs near the Maqam Ibrahim (peace be upon him) or in the Hijr, then sit until the sun declines. Then pray the obligatory prayer. Then say in the aftermath of your prayer as you said when you entered the state of ihram from al-Shajara: 'I enter the state of ihram for Hajj.' Then proceed, with calmness and dignity upon you. And when you reach al-Raqta' before al-Radm, say 'Labbayk'. And when you reach al-Radm and look out over al-Abtah, raise your voice with the Talbiyah until you arrive at Mina."

key_terms.اَلتَّلْبِيَةُ: The Talbiyah (chant of 'Here I am, O God')
key_terms.يَوْمُ اَلتَّرْوِيَةِ: Day of Tarwiah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What are the steps for entering ihram for Hajj on the Day of Tarwiah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* details the Sunnah of entering ihram on the 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah, emphasizing the spiritual demeanor of *sakinah* (tranquility) and *waqar* (dignity) throughout the transition from Mecca to Mina. It highlights the specific ritual sequence of bathing, praying at the Maqam Ibrahim, and formally declaring the Hajj intention, while prescribing the gradual increase in the volume of the *talbiyah* as the pilgrim approaches the sacred boundaries, reflecting the gradual intensification of the pilgrimage state.
